_doc: Candidate DRAWING VOCABULARIES: genuinely different ways to draw the same scene (a person, a horse, a vault, three coins, a tree). Each is authored in styles/vocabularies.html as its own set of draw functions with its own natural pen. The pen axis (styles.json) can be re-applied later to whichever vocabulary Mike picks. Mike (2026-10-30): keep EVERY candidate as an option (a multi-chapter video may want dark mode in one chapter, light in another); status 'current' marks today's pick, status_note keeps his remarks.

vocabularies.name: Hand-drawn with hair
vocabularies.blurb: Round heads, hair variants, tapered shirts, stick limbs, an illustrated horse with mane and hooves, ground shadows. Wobbly ink, flat pastel fills.
vocabularies.status_note: Mike, 2026-10-30: the pick for the first demo (with paper-pastel)

vocabularies.name: Bean characters
vocabularies.blurb: No necks: tall pill bodies with the face on the body, stubby arms and legs, a plump horse with tufted mane and tail. Clean thin outline, rounded everything.

vocabularies.name: Geometric flat
vocabularies.blurb: No outlines, no faces: circle heads, rounded-rectangle torsos, thick rounded limbs; the horse built from rounded blocks. Two tones per object, corporate-flat.
vocabularies.status_note: Mike, 2026-10-30: does not want the other vocabularies

vocabularies.name: Pictogram glyphs
vocabularies.blurb: Everything a solid one-color silhouette like airport signage; one accent color marks the thing that matters. Zero texture, maximum legibility at small size.

vocabularies.name: Isometric blocks
vocabularies.blurb: Every object is a three-tone cuboid on an isometric grid: a boxy horse, a cube vault, cylinder coins, a low-poly tree. Reads as a tiny 3D diorama without any 3D package.

vocabularies.name: Pixel art
vocabularies.blurb: Sprites on a 22 px cell grid, hard edges, a small fixed palette, bitmap heading. Instantly recognizable and cheap to author as text maps.

vocabularies.name: Pure line art
vocabularies.blurb: Ink outlines only, no fills anywhere, a single accent color for emphasis. Elegant and fast to read; everything stays an outline.
vocabularies.status_note: Mike, 2026-10-30: does not want the other vocabularies
